draft.change: Add the exhortative sense come-now to the Hebrew Qal of יָהַב.
draft.definition: The imperative הָבָה introduces a proposal and urges the hearer to act with the speaker.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 11:3, הָבָה introduces נִלְבְּנָה, “let us make bricks,” followed by וְנִשְׂרְפָה, “and let us burn them.” Both cohortatives express the shared undertaking.

analysis.evidence: הָבָה introduces two first-person plural cohortatives, נֵרְדָה ‘let us go down’ and וְנָבְלָה ‘and let us confuse [their language]’. It urges the hearer to join in both actions.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine singular, with final paragogic ה.
analysis.sense: Urge the hearer to join the speaker in a proposed action.

analysis.evidence: Yahweh introduces the proposal with הָבָה, “come,” and pairs נֵרְדָה with וְנָבְלָה שָׁם, “and let us confuse their language there.” The two cohortatives express his proposal to descend and act there.
analysis.morphology: Qal cohortative, first person common plural, with the prefix נ־ and the cohortative ending ־ָה.

analysis.evidence: נֵרְדָה means “let us go down,” and וְנָבְלָה continues the proposal. Its object is שְׂפָתָם, “their language.” The purpose is that people will no longer understand one another’s speech.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins two Qal first-person common plural cohortatives. The prefix נ־ marks the first-person plural, and the ending ־ָה marks the cohortative.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68354:8, 66060:4, 66059:10, 66056:7.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׂפָתָם is the object of וְנָבְלָה, “let us confuse.” The intended result is that each person will no longer understand the language of the other, so the noun denotes their shared language.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine plural possessive suffix.
